task: Night research round 3, scan_hypotheses: honest use of the 26-27 Sep slots before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC), with F1 = K2 and F2 = the exp58n twin fixed and every lab rider closed. Focus: (a) evidence that does not depend on the public embryo, (b) K2 vs twin by embryo and density quartile on the exp60 lab, (c) what the 0.954-0.957 teams do, (d) gaps in the finals rule.
summary: Everything was measured on the existing exp60 dumps (56 clips, official matching), the dummy logs and the Kaggle CLI (read-only). No GPU was used; scripts are in the session scratchpad. (b) The insertion is not a dense-clip risk. Its lab gain (an in-sample upper bound) comes mostly from sparse clips: Q0 +0.0246, Q1 +0.0028, Q2 -0.0005, Q3 +0.0019. The dense half gets 1 TP and 3 FP, which is still above the lab break-even precision q* = J/(1+J) = 0.114. 93% of the 201 inserted forks are ignored by the metric. So no density gate is warranted, and the private risk of the insertion needs an out-of-fold evaluable precision below ~11%, against 60% in-sample. (a) No tail lever is left that is honest and does not depend on the public embryo. The x138 final graphs are structurally clean: 0 isolated nodes, 0 nodes with more than 2 children, 0 multi-parent nodes, 0 edges with dt != 1, and about 190 near-duplicate node pairs out of ~1.1 M nodes. There are 0 mutual-nearest end->start pairs within 7 um that could be bridged. Switching between the dual-seed retention-guard modes carries no boundary penalty. The remaining edge FN (1,705 of 40,093 GT edges) are 49% detector misses, 43% swaps (the parent is linked to another child) and 8% dangling ends. All of that needs retraining, which R9 forbids. The lowrefine code already has finite, clip and 2 um bound guards, and its GPU cost is ~0 s. The ILP timeout margin is 15x. (c) No new public kernel has run since 25 Sep 09:09 UTC. At 22:23 UTC we are #164 of 3,914. The 0.954 block covers ranks 147-211, and the silver line (~196) is 32 ranks below us. The number of teams at >= 0.954 grows by ~3.8 per hour. (d) The real remaining gap is lowrefine. F1 and F2 both carry it, it has no honest lab, and its only reads will be K2 - #35 and twin - #34 on the public embryo (~06:30-08:00 UTC). The rules do not say what happens if K2 <= 0.952: R3 drops lowrefine, but K1 is unscored and approved only if K2 errors. They also clash if the twin shows 0.952: the f2 floor of 0.953 disagrees with R3's -0.001 tolerance. Both branches should be pre-registered before the scores appear. Recommendation: declare the new-mechanism search closed now rather than at R8. The 26-27 Sep slots stay empty except for the conditional K1 (and floatout in S12 if the user OKs it).

findings.what: Pre-register the lowrefine read before K2 and the twin score (expected ~06:30-08:00 UTC 26 Sep). Three facts set this up. safetail is inert when no deadline fires (the K1 dummy sha256 equals the exp57b dummy). The insertion is identical in K2 and #35, and the twin and #34 both lack it. So d1 = K2 - #35 (0.954) and d2 = twin - #34 (0.953) are both public reads of lowrefine alone. lowrefine has NO honest lab: the exp60 base has no lowrefine, and the dummy's +0.0025 comes only from head-train stem 6bba_05db0fb1. Two gaps follow. GAP 1: if d1 <= -0.002, R3 drops lowrefine and F1 must become K1 (exp58t v1, x138 + safetail + gated insertion). But K1 is unscored, and its submit is approved only if K2 ERRORS (round 1 item 6). GAP 2: f2 admits the twin only if public >= 0.953, yet R3 keeps a -0.001 rider. A twin at 0.952 would therefore swap F2 to exp52 (0.950), which is 3 below it, while F1 still carries the same lowrefine. Proposed text (tightening and slot-use, [OK] for the K1 submit): 'LOWREFINE READ (written before K2/twin scores): d1 = K2 - #35 decides by R3; d1 <= -0.002 -> lowrefine dropped, K1 (exp58t v1, gated) submitted in the next 26 Sep slot, F1 = K1 once scored + R5-admissible, F2 = exp52 (the twin carries the rejected rider; exp58nt would be a byte-copy of x138 and is never ticked). d1 >= -0.001 -> lowrefine kept; then the twin stays F2 when twin >= 0.952 (the R3 tolerance), otherwise exp52. d2 alone never drops lowrefine (the same embryo and mostly the same nodes, so it is not an independent read).'

findings.what: Private-robustness read of the insertion (K2 vs twin) by density quartile and embryo on the exp60 lab. Quartiles are cut on control nodes/frame at 83.7 / 160.7 / 258.8, 14 clips each. ins35 score delta and division TP/FP/FN: Q0 +0.0246 (4/1/21 -> 11/3/14), Q1 +0.0028 (6/3/18 -> 7/4/17), Q2 -0.0005 (3/6/20 -> 3/7/20), Q3 +0.0019 (3/15/24 -> 4/17/23); ALL +0.0065 (16/25/83 -> 25/31/74). By embryo: 44b6 +0.0058, all from ONE TP on 44b6_d754aa59, with 54 of its 55 inserted forks ignored; 6bba +0.0065 (8 TP, 6 FP). The per-video cap of 4 binds on most clips, so the insertion COUNT does not depend on density, but its precision does: the sparse half gives 8 TP / 3 FP, the dense half 1 TP / 3 FP. Even the dense half (0.25) is above the lab break-even q* = J/(1+J) = 0.129/1.129 = 0.114. Of the 201 inserted forks, 186 (93%) are metric-ignored. Arithmetic for private harm: with 15 evaluable inserted forks at base 16/25/83, 2 TP / 13 FP gives J 0.131 (still >= 0.129) and 1 TP / 14 FP gives J 0.123. The insertion therefore hurts only if its out-of-fold evaluable precision is below ~11%, against 60% in-sample (L5 upper bound). The dense clips (Q2-Q3 are where 44b6/6bba scores are lowest) are not a special risk.

findings.what: Where the x138 lab errors actually sit, and why no post-processing lever is left before R8. Of the pooled GT edges (40,093), 1,705 are FN (4.25%). 834 (49%) are node misses (an endpoint has no matched prediction). 730 (43%) are swaps (both endpoints matched, but the predicted parent is linked to another child). Only 141 (8%) are dangling ends (the predicted parent has no child at all). Mutual-nearest-neighbour pairs of a predicted end at t and a predicted start at t+1 within 2, 3, 4, 5 or 7 um number ZERO on all 56 clips, because x138's relink/gapfill already bridges them. Node misses need the detector and swaps need the edge model; both mean retraining, which R9 forbids. RE-AIM (Corwin) already showed that flow re-solving is a no-op on x138 (2 of 117,077 edges). This is the structural reason the fork family, ANTIPAR, forkblob, forkmid, the DeepCenter threshold and tempfuse all ended at ~0: the tail is saturated.

findings.what: No penalty for flicker between the dual-seed retention-guard modes; closed. x138 switches each frame between the blended (primary + secondary) and primary-only candidates when blended/primary retention < 0.9. 20 of the 56 lab clips mix the two modes, and 2 (44b6_9be80b04, 44b6_e28840c6) are 100% primary. GT-edge FN rates by frame pair: clips that are all blended 4.16% (24,572 edges); in mixed clips, blended-blended 3.17% (12,156), primary-primary 10.71% (1,960) and switch pairs 6.05% (876); all-primary clips 6.43% (529). Switch pairs fall between the two modes, so there is no boundary effect. The high primary-frame FN rate is a selection effect: those are the frames where the secondary drops candidates, i.e. hard frames. A hysteresis or per-movie-scope rule would change the node set (R4), would need a GPU lab and has no measured target. Not proposed.

findings.what: Re-checked that the finals pair still hedges what it should, after round 3's measurements. F2 (twin) hedges the insertion; the insertion's private-harm threshold (OOF evaluable precision < ~11%) is far below its in-sample 60%, so the hedge is cheap insurance and not a likely switch. The unhedged common mode of F1 and F2 is lowrefine + safetail. safetail is proven inert without a deadline and fail-soft (FD/FF dummies). lowrefine is the only shared component whose sign rests on public reads alone, hence R3S-1/R3S-7. Nothing else is shared that could fail both: the lowrefine code guards against NaN and out-of-volume shifts and costs no runtime. The insertion (8.0 h) and repair (9.5 h) deadlines apply only to F1's insertion path. The twin repairs in ~219 s against K2's 509 s on the dummy, so the twin cannot time out where K2 does not. Round 1's rejection of D4 (two-stage exact insertion scoring) stays correct: it pays only if L(K2) > 8.0 h, which the A5 ledger reports.
